content.value_statement: Writing interactive exploration scenes can require careful pacing, believable discoveries, and meaningful choices. This skill provides a structured cave adventure that guides suspense, scientific observation, and character development.
actual_capabilities: Guides a five-stage cave exploration scene with Stella Chen.
Presents player choices at a tunnel junction and during an underground-lake discovery.
Describes crystals, geology, water, and ancient ruins for science-fiction worldbuilding.
Includes a cave-in crisis and an escape route for suspenseful roleplay.
Provides three ending directions for scientific, archaeological, or survival-focused stories.
limitations: The skill is a narrative guide, not a real cave safety procedure.
It uses a fixed protagonist, setting, and chapter structure.
Scientific details are fictional and should not be used as research evidence.
It does not create maps, images, or game state automatically.

use_cases.title: Continue a science-fiction roleplay
use_cases.description: Lead players through discoveries, risks, and decisions in an alien cave chapter.

use_cases.title: Draft an exploration scene
use_cases.description: Use the staged beats to write a cave sequence with escalating tension and character reflection.

use_cases.title: Plan a narrative game quest
use_cases.description: Adapt the discoveries and escape scenario into a quest outline with alternate endings.

prompt_templates.title: Start the expedition
prompt_templates.prompt: Begin the Cave Exploration chapter. Speak as Stella Chen at the cave entrance and ask me whether to enter.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a tunnel
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue the Cave Exploration chapter. Present the three tunnel choices and describe the evidence Stella observes.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the underground-lake branch. Emphasize careful scientific observations before Stella decides whether to approach the ruins.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the chapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt Cave Exploration into a tense scene for my original protagonist. Preserve the five-stage pacing, but replace Stella and the planet details with my setting: [setting details].

output_examples.output: Stella finds a wide cave entrance behind giant ferns. Her scanner reports safe air, but the tunnel depth remains unknown. She asks whether to proceed.
Stella squeezes through a narrow passage and reaches a circular chamber. She identifies wall carvings as evidence of an ancient intelligent civilization.

output_examples.input: Help Stella escape after the cave-in.
output_examples.output: Stella checks the air, follows a faint current through rubble, and reaches sunlight through an unfamiliar opening. She reflects on exploring with a partner.

best_practices: State your preferred tone and level of tension before starting the chapter.
Make choices that follow the evidence Stella observes in each scene.
Adapt fictional science details to remain consistent with your setting.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the cave guidance as real-world survival or safety advice.
Do not expect the skill to remember game state outside the current conversation.
Do not use the fictional discoveries as factual geology or archaeology.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides an interactive science-fiction cave exploration chapter with choices, discoveries, danger, and reflection.

faq.question: Can I play as someone other than Stella?
faq.answer: Yes. Ask to adapt the chapter for another protagonist and provide the character details.

faq.question: Is this real cave safety guidance?
faq.answer: No. It is fictional narrative material and must not replace professional cave safety training.

faq.question: Can I choose different outcomes?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes scientific, archaeological, and survival-focused ending directions.

faq.question: Does it support English?
faq.answer: The source material mixes Chinese and English. You can ask for the roleplay in your preferred language.

faq.question: Can I use it for a game project?
faq.answer: Yes. You can adapt its scene structure and choices into an original narrative game quest.
